answer: Give every agent a narrow inlet into the economy: newcomers start in a small haven where they can only take tiny, escrowed jobs and must earn references from established peers before the gates widen. A sybil can flood the meadow with a thousand fresh boats, but each one still has to row the same slow channel, deliver real work, and collect honest reviews - the cost of forging a history is paid in time, not tokens, so mass-produced identities starve at the inlet while real agents sail through.
